Return only one complete, self-contained IEC 61131-3 Structured Text FUNCTION_BLOCK implementation, including all VAR sections and END_FUNCTION_BLOCK. Use the exact input/output/inout names, types, directions and behavior in the user task. Use FUNCTION_BLOCK (not PROGRAM) for every task in this benchmark. Necessary named TYPE definitions may precede the block. Keep helper state inside VAR; do not emit nested FUNCTION/METHOD/ACTION or workspace-inspection commentary. Use supported standard ST constructs and explicit type conversions. Avoid CODESYS reserved local identifiers s and r; use SHL/SHR functions for shifts. Return a single fenced st block, without explanatory prose outside ST comments. Do not inspect files or request tools. The user task remains verbatim; these are shared packaging/output requirements for both frameworks. Target CODESYS 3.5 ST. End IF/CASE/FOR/WHILE/REPEAT statements with semicolons. In a CODESYS DUT, the top-level END_STRUCT is directly followed by END_TYPE; do not insert a semicolon between them. Nested STRUCT field declarations keep their required separators. Use ELSIF for a flat conditional chain; preserve balanced END_IF for true nested conditionals. Declare every enum and helper variable. Do not use AT located declarations in this function block. RETURN is a bare statement; assign declared outputs before RETURN, never RETURN an expression. Preserve exact interface types including UINT, LTIME and VARIANT; do not narrow or replace them. Respect stated latching and scan behavior; do not add unstated edge-only triggers, resets or interlocks. Keep reasoning concise and emit only the implementation.
Before implementing, put a concise ENGINEERING_CONTRACT comment inside the ST block (up to 12 lines). For each output or state group state: activation, retention/hold, explicit reset/deactivation, same-scan priority, and units/boundaries. Cite PUB clause IDs where relevant. This is a reviewable design table, not a reasoning transcript. Use only the task's public requirements. Preserve output state when the task explicitly requires retention; do not assume a mutually exclusive state machine automatically shuts down earlier outputs. Do not invent resets, interlocks, edge triggers or operation priorities. Mark unspecified details as unspecified and implement a consistent interpretation. Check strict > versus >=, boundary scan timing, TIME milliseconds versus LTIME nanoseconds, zero/reset behavior, array slot versus stored identifier and simultaneous operations when applicable. Return the table as an ST comment followed by the complete implementation in the same single fenced ST block. Missing table is recorded as process compliance, not a functional scoring failure. Also emit a separate ST comment (* CONTRACT_RULES [...] *) containing a JSON list for any unconditional public Boolean output latch explicitly required by the task. Each supported rule has kind=hold_until_reset, output=<public BOOL output>, set_input=<public BOOL input>, reset_input=<public BOOL input or null>. Use [] when no such unconditional latch is specified. The checker executes these declarations on generated public-input traces; do not declare conditions the implementation does not satisfy. These checks supplement the task and do not change its scoring.
Target tools: CODESYS 3.5 native compilation; deterministic local scan interpreter; bounded LTL checking after functional success. Supported core: IF/ELSIF, nested CASE, FOR/WHILE/REPEAT, named or anonymous integer enums, declared STRUCT/ARRAY, TIME/LTIME, TON, R_TRIG/F_TRIG, bit selectors, SHL/SHR, explicit IEC conversions and exact generic TO_BOOL/integer/bit conversions. Prefer explicit source_TO_target conversions, especially for REAL. Declare helper types and functions before use; avoid external library helpers unless supplied by the task. Keep every original public interface type and field spelling. Tool limits never authorize changing the task interface. Do not replace LTIME with floating-point arithmetic or VARIANT with DINT. CODESYS STRING scalar indexing is zero-based and returns BYTE, not a one-character STRING. For ASCII text, iterate byte indices 0 through LEN(text)-1, or use MID(text,1,position) with one-based position to get a one-character STRING. Do not mix those indexing conventions. Whole STRUCT and ARRAY assignments copy values. Generic TO_LREAL accepts numeric/BOOL operands; TO_REAL rounds to IEEE binary32. R_TRIG/F_TRIG and TON keep state across calls. On same-scan state changes determine the final timer enable before calling the timer so a newly enabled output and its elapsed-time origin agree. When multiple command inputs are asserted, preserve the public operation contracts or explicitly report an unsupported combination through an existing error interface; do not silently drop commands through an arbitrary priority. Prefix helper local names with tmp_ or local_ to avoid collisions with standard functions and reserved words, including LEN, S and R. Never shadow a standard function that the block calls.

# Automated Filling Line Control

- **Difficulty:** Easy (easy)

## Requirements

An automated filling line responsible for cleaning, filling, capping, and packaging bottles. Each step of the production line is controlled by PLC and triggered by signals from sensors and operators.
Control requirements:
When the sensor bottleSensor detects a bottle, it triggers the start of the cleaning pump and continues to work.
After cleaning is completed, the operator operates the button cleaningConfirmButton to trigger the cleaning completion signal, automatically starting the filling valve for filling.
After filling is completed, the operator operates the button fillingConfirmButton to trigger the filling completion signal, automatically starting the capping machine for capping.
After capping is completed, the operator operates the button cappingConfirmButton to trigger the capping completion signal, starting the packing machine for packaging.
After packaging is completed, the operator operates the button packingConfirmButton to trigger the packaging completion signal, lighting up the packaging completion indicator light.
After the operator picks up the packaged bottle, they press the confirmation button finishedButton to reset the indicator light and prepare for the next bottle's production cycle.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `bottleSensor` | `BOOL` | The bottle reaches the sensor, triggering a signal when a bottle is detected |
| Input | `cleaningConfirmButton` | `BOOL` | Operator confirmation button, used to confirm the completion of the cleaning process |
| Input | `fillingConfirmButton` | `BOOL` | Operator confirmation button, used to confirm the completion of the filling process |
| Input | `cappingConfirmButton` | `BOOL` | Operator confirmation button, used to confirm the completion of the capping process |
| Input | `packingConfirmButton` | `BOOL` | Operator confirmation button, used to confirm the completion of the packaging process |
| Input | `finishedButton` | `BOOL` | Operator confirmation button, used to confirm that the bottle has been picked up |
| Output | `Pump_Motor` | `BOOL` | Control output for the operation of the cleaning pump motor |
| Output | `Filling_Valve` | `BOOL` | Control output for the operation of the filling valve |
| Output | `Capping_Machine` | `BOOL` | Control output for the operation of the capping machine |
| Output | `Packing_Machine` | `BOOL` | Control output for the operation of the packing machine |
| Output | `Completion_Light` | `BOOL` | Indicator light for packaging completion |
